method: Falsifiable calls about points/loyalty landscape movement — bonuses expected to return, devaluations expected to land, sweet spots expected to close. Each has a concrete test and a real horizon date. Misses recorded honestly.

calls.call: The current Chase Ultimate Rewards → IHG One Rewards 70% transfer bonus (expiring 2026-08-31) will NOT be extended or replaced with any Chase→IHG transfer bonus before 2026-10-31.
calls.basis: Chase already stepped this promo down once — from a 100% early-bird (Jul 15-30) to 70% (Jul 31-Aug 31). Stepping down mid-campaign is a cool-off signal, not a warm-up. Historically Chase has left 3-6 month gaps between IHG promos.
calls.test: GRADE HIT if no Chase→IHG transfer bonus of any percentage is publicly offered between 2026-09-01 and 2026-10-31. GRADE MISS if any Chase→IHG bonus (>0%) is announced or live during that window.

calls.call: U.S. Bank will restore either Air France/KLM Flying Blue OR Qantas Frequent Flyer as an Altitude Reserve transfer partner by 2026-10-25.
calls.basis: Both partners went live on 2026-08-11 and were pulled roughly 24 hours later on 2026-08-12; Frequent Miler, Doctor of Credit and One Mile at a Time all characterise the removal as IT-integration failure rather than deal collapse. U.S. Bank waited eight months past its own December 2025 target to ship transfers at all — reputational cost of leaving these missing is high, and bank IT integration fixes typically land in 2–6 weeks. 10 weeks is a generous horizon.
calls.test: GRADE HIT if, at any point between 2026-08-16 and 2026-10-25 inclusive, either Air France/KLM Flying Blue or Qantas Frequent Flyer is publicly listed as an active transfer partner in the U.S. Bank Rewards Center for the Altitude Reserve card, evidenced by U.S. Bank's own transfer page or a Tier 1 confirmation. GRADE MISS if neither partner has been restored by end of day 2026-10-25 Pacific time.

calls.call: Citi will re-run its ThankYou → Air France/KLM Flying Blue transfer bonus at 20% or higher between 2026-08-23 and 2026-11-15.
calls.basis: The current Citi→Flying Blue 20% bonus expires August 22, 2026. Historical cadence: Citi ran Flying Blue bonuses in February 2026, May 2026, and August 2026 — a roughly 3-month cadence. If the pattern holds, the next window opens in early-to-mid November, well inside the horizon. Citi has strong commercial reasons to keep Flying Blue front-of-mind: it is one of the more useful ThankYou partners for European redemption and a key reason to keep the Citi Strata Premier open.
calls.test: GRADE HIT if any Citi ThankYou → Air France/KLM Flying Blue transfer bonus of 20% or greater is publicly offered at any point between 2026-08-23 and 2026-11-15 inclusive, evidenced by Citi's own transfer page, Flying Blue's promo page, or a Tier 1/Tier 2 confirmation. GRADE MISS if no such bonus is offered in that window.

calls.call: Citi ThankYou will run another transfer bonus to Turkish Airlines Miles & Smiles of 30% or higher between 2026-09-01 and 2026-11-30.
calls.basis: Citi's current Turkish 40% bonus (ending 2026-08-31) is the third Citi→Turkish promo of 2026; the program has a clear quarterly cadence. Turkish devalued domestic Star Alliance awards in December 2025 but LEFT the region-to-region chart alone — partner business class North America→Europe still starts at 65,000 miles, which remains one of the strongest sweet spots reachable via a US bank transfer. Citi has commercial incentive to keep pushing this partner because it is the largest single reason to hold Strata Premier for a value-focused points user. A 12-week silence would break a well-established pattern.
calls.test: GRADE HIT if any Citi ThankYou → Turkish Airlines Miles & Smiles transfer bonus of 30% or greater is publicly offered at any point between 2026-09-01 and 2026-11-30 inclusive, evidenced by Citi's transfer page, Turkish's promo page, or a Tier 1/Tier 2 confirmation. GRADE MISS if no such bonus is offered in that window.

calls.call: Amex Membership Rewards will run another transfer bonus of 25% or higher to at least one Avios program (British Airways, Iberia, or Aer Lingus) between 2026-09-28 and 2026-12-31.
calls.basis: Amex has run 30%+ Avios bonuses on a roughly semi-annual cadence for years, and the current 30% bonus (expiring 2026-09-27) is well established as a routine promotion. The Avios family sits at the centre of Amex's transfer stack because Iberia short-haul to Madrid and single-partner AA short-haul remain two of the strongest sweet spots reachable directly from Membership Rewards. A three-month silence after this bonus ends would break a multi-year pattern; a repeat before year-end is the base case.
calls.test: GRADE HIT if any Amex Membership Rewards → British Airways, Iberia, or Aer Lingus Avios transfer bonus of 25% or greater is publicly offered at any point between 2026-09-28 and 2026-12-31 inclusive, evidenced by Amex's own transfer page, an Avios program promo page, or a Tier 1/Tier 2 confirmation. GRADE MISS if no such bonus is offered in that window.

calls.call: Chase will NOT offer a Chase Ultimate Rewards → World of Hyatt transfer bonus of any percentage at any point between 2026-08-22 and 2027-02-28.
calls.basis: Since the UR→Hyatt transfer partnership launched with Hyatt as Chase's sole hotel transfer partner (October 2018), Chase has never once offered a bonus on this route — the 1:1 rate has been treated as sacrosanct. Hyatt is by consensus the most valuable single destination in the Chase transferable stack, and both parties benefit commercially from keeping the ratio boring: Hyatt gets sticky earned-balance transfers, Chase gets a durable 'points worth ~2 cents' value narrative. Even after Hyatt's May 2026 chart devaluation weakened the round-trip case at top-band aspirational properties, no bonus has been floated. A first-ever Chase→Hyatt bonus inside six months would break an eight-year pattern and would be one of the largest structural changes in the transferable-points landscape.
calls.test: GRADE HIT if no Chase Ultimate Rewards → World of Hyatt transfer bonus of any percentage is publicly offered at any point between 2026-08-22 and 2027-02-28 inclusive. GRADE MISS if any such bonus (>0%) is announced or live during that window, evidenced by Chase's own transfer page and confirmed by at least one Tier 1 or Tier 2 source.

calls.call: Capital One will run another Capital One miles → Avianca LifeMiles transfer bonus of 20% or higher between 2026-10-01 and 2026-12-31.
calls.basis: Capital One has run LifeMiles bonuses on a roughly quarterly cadence through 2026 (February, May, August), typically in the 15-25% range. The current 15% promo ends 2026-08-31, and Q4 is Capital One's historically most active bonus window as it competes for year-end transfer volume against Amex's Avios push. LifeMiles remains one of the top three redemption destinations for Capital One miles thanks to distance-based Star Alliance pricing (25,000 for US-domestic short-haul in business; 63,000 US→Europe in business) and no fuel surcharges on Star partners. A three-month silence after August would break a multi-year cadence.
calls.test: GRADE HIT if any Capital One miles → Avianca LifeMiles transfer bonus of 20% or greater is publicly offered at any point between 2026-10-01 and 2026-12-31 inclusive, evidenced by Capital One's own transfer page, Avianca's promo page, or a Tier 1/Tier 2 confirmation. GRADE MISS if no such bonus is offered in that window.

calls.call: The Chase Ultimate Rewards → Air Canada Aeroplan 20% bonus (live, expiring 2026-09-30) will be Chase's LAST UR → airline transfer bonus of 2026 — no additional Chase UR → airline bonus will be publicly offered between 2026-10-01 and 2026-12-31.
calls.basis: Chase is structurally the least promotional of the transferable-points banks on airlines: 2025 saw only two UR → airline bonuses (Aeroplan and Emirates), and 2026 has so far delivered exactly one (Aeroplan, currently live). Chase's Q4 pattern favours hotel partners — IHG, Marriott — and leaves airline promo season to Amex (Avios) and Citi (Turkish, Flying Blue). Aeroplan is Chase's default airline handshake and, with it running now, the airline box is arguably checked for the year. This call bets on Chase's revealed preference not to compete on airline transfers in Q4.
calls.test: GRADE HIT if no Chase Ultimate Rewards → airline transfer bonus of any percentage (any Chase UR airline transfer partner: United, Aeroplan, British Airways, Iberia, Aer Lingus, Emirates, Singapore, JetBlue, Southwest, Virgin Atlantic) is publicly offered at any point between 2026-10-01 and 2026-12-31 inclusive. GRADE MISS if any such bonus (>0%) is announced or live during that window, evidenced by Chase's own transfer page and confirmed by at least one Tier 1 or Tier 2 source.

calls.call: Cathay Pacific will run another multi-bank Asia Miles transfer bonus of 10% or higher (from any of Amex MR, Citi ThankYou, Capital One, Bilt, Wells Fargo, or Brex) between 2026-11-01 and 2027-01-31.
calls.basis: Cathay has run at least one all-partner US transfer promotion in Q4 of each of the last two years — Q4 2024 was a 30% bonus, Q4 2025 was 20%. The current multi-partner 10% (registration-required, capped at 10,000 bonus miles, expires 2026-08-28) is Cathay's Q3 push and is structurally quieter than prior efforts, but Cathay has strong commercial reasons to return in Q4 as Asia holiday-travel bookings peak and Hong Kong's high season begins. Cathay's Asia Miles balance sheet needs the transfer inflow because its own earn engine (co-brand cards, partner airlines) has been shrinking relative to peers. A four-month silence after Aug 28 would break a two-year Q4 pattern.
calls.test: GRADE HIT if any Cathay Pacific Asia Miles transfer bonus of 10% or greater is publicly offered from any of Amex MR, Citi ThankYou, Capital One, Bilt, Wells Fargo, or Brex at any point between 2026-11-01 and 2027-01-31 inclusive, evidenced by Cathay's own promo page or a Tier 1/Tier 2 confirmation. GRADE MISS if no such bonus is offered from any of those six programs in that window.

calls.call: The next Cathay Pacific Asia Miles all-partner US transfer bonus (from any of Amex MR, Citi ThankYou, Capital One, Bilt, Wells Fargo, or Brex) offered after 2026-08-28 will match or tighten current terms rather than revert to prior Q4 generosity — it will land at 10% or lower, OR it will cap total bonus miles at 15,000 or fewer per member.
calls.basis: Cathay's US all-partner conversion bonus has degraded monotonically for three years running: Q4 2024 was 30% uncapped, Q4 2025 was 20% uncapped, and the current Aug 2026 promo is 10% with a hard 10,000-bonus-mile cap plus a registration requirement. Cathay's own earning engine (co-brand cards outside Hong Kong, partner-airline earning) has been contracting relative to peers, so heavy uncapped US transfer promos have become harder to justify commercially. The Aug 2026 terms look like Cathay establishing a new floor, not an anomalous cutback. A return to Q4 2024/2025 generosity would represent a policy reversal.
calls.test: GRADE HIT if the next Cathay Pacific Asia Miles all-partner (Amex MR, Citi ThankYou, Capital One, Bilt, Wells Fargo, or Brex) US transfer bonus publicly offered between 2026-08-29 and 2027-01-31 inclusive is either (a) at 10% or lower, OR (b) caps total bonus miles at 15,000 or fewer per member. GRADE MISS if the next such bonus is above 10% AND is either uncapped or capped above 15,000 bonus miles per member. GRADE UNSETTLED if no all-partner Cathay bonus is offered in that window.

calls.call: Amex Membership Rewards will run another transfer bonus of 30% or higher to Virgin Atlantic Flying Club between 2026-10-01 and 2027-01-31.
calls.basis: The last Amex→Virgin Atlantic bonus was 30% for the whole of July 2026 (Jul 1–31), and Amex has run at least one Virgin Atlantic bonus every year since the partnership began. Virgin Atlantic is Amex's exclusive US transfer route to Delta-partner Virgin space and to ANA First (via Virgin miles), giving Amex durable commercial reason to keep promoting it. Q4 into January is Amex's most active bonus window as it competes with Citi and Capital One for year-end transfer volume. A five-month silence between August and end-January would break a multi-year cadence; a return in the Oct–Jan window is the base case.
calls.test: GRADE HIT if any Amex Membership Rewards → Virgin Atlantic Flying Club transfer bonus of 30% or greater is publicly offered at any point between 2026-10-01 and 2027-01-31 inclusive, evidenced by Amex's own transfer page, Virgin Atlantic's promo page, or a Tier 1/Tier 2 confirmation. GRADE MISS if no such bonus is offered in that window.

calls.call: World of Hyatt will publicly launch at least one system-wide Bonus Journeys or equivalent points-earning promotion (2x base points or higher on paid stays) with a booking or stay window that falls entirely between 2026-09-15 and 2026-12-31.
calls.basis: Hyatt has published a Bonus Journeys promotion in each of the last three calendar quarters and in each of the last three Q4 windows, with typical structure 2x base points on stays booked in a defined window and completed within ~90 days. After the May 2026 award-chart devaluation weakened the redemption side, Hyatt's commercial incentive is to keep engagement flowing through earn-side promotions rather than transfer bonuses (see call 2026-08-22-1 on the sacrosanct 1:1 Chase→Hyatt line). Q4 in particular targets pre-holiday leisure and end-of-year corporate stays — skipping it would break a multi-year cadence.
calls.test: GRADE HIT if World of Hyatt publicly launches a Bonus Journeys or equivalent points-earning promotion (2x base points or higher on paid stays) whose booking window OR stay window falls entirely between 2026-09-15 and 2026-12-31, evidenced by hyatt.com/en-US/world-of-hyatt/promotions (Tier 1) or a Tier 1/Tier 2 confirmation. GRADE MISS if no such promo is publicly available in that window.

calls.call: None of the four major bank transferable-points programs — Amex Membership Rewards, Chase Ultimate Rewards, Citi ThankYou, or Capital One Miles — will add Alaska/Hawaiian Atmos Rewards as a publicly listed transfer partner between 2026-08-29 and 2027-02-28.
calls.basis: Alaska completed operational integration with Hawaiian on 2026-08-14 and consolidated HawaiianMiles and Mileage Plan into a single Atmos Rewards balance, arguably making Atmos a more attractive single partner than either predecessor. But Alaska Air Group's VP of Loyalty has publicly stated that major bank programs 'are ultimately competitors', and the closure of the Amex→Hawaiian route on 2025-06-30 removed the last indirect bank→Alaska path. Bilt and Marriott Bonvoy remain the only routes in; neither Chase nor Amex has ever had Alaska as a direct transfer partner. A first-ever Amex/Chase/Citi/Cap-One→Atmos partnership inside six months would require reversing a publicly stated 'they are competitors' posture from loyalty leadership — that kind of reversal typically takes longer than six months to negotiate, sign, and announce, even when interest exists. Bilt is excluded because that partnership already exists at 1:1.
calls.test: GRADE HIT if none of Amex Membership Rewards, Chase Ultimate Rewards, Citi ThankYou, or Capital One Miles publicly lists Alaska/Hawaiian Atmos Rewards as an active transfer partner at any point between 2026-08-29 and 2027-02-28 inclusive. GRADE MISS if any of those four programs adds Atmos Rewards as a publicly listed transfer partner in that window, evidenced by the bank's own transfer page and confirmed by at least one Tier 1 or Tier 2 source.

calls.call: Air Canada Aeroplan will NOT publicly announce any member-negative change to its award chart pricing, partner transfer ratios, partner earning ratios, or elite qualification thresholds in the six months following the Blackstone/La Caisse minority investment settlement — between 2026-08-30 and 2027-02-28 inclusive.
calls.basis: The August 11 deal (settled August 17) gives Blackstone-led investors a 25% non-controlling stake at a $10B valuation while Air Canada retains 75% ownership and 'full operational control' over strategy, day-to-day management and financial consolidation. Media coverage has floated devaluation risk as the primary concern, but private-equity minority investments in loyalty programs (Aimia's original private-equity phase, prior IAG Loyalty deals, points-industry precedents) typically manifest programmatic effects over multi-year timelines rather than first-quarter announcements. Aeroplan's 2026 product roadmap — including its new revenue-based earning integration and the Chase UR 20% bonus running through Sep 30 — was locked before this deal closed. A six-month horizon lets that roadmap play out; devaluation-driven change coming inside that window would represent a much faster investor-pressure response than the historical base rate suggests. This is a contrarian call — the loud consensus is that this deal is bad for members. HIT means the loud consensus was premature; MISS means it was right.
calls.test: GRADE HIT if Air Canada / Aeroplan does not publicly announce, at any point between 2026-08-30 and 2027-02-28 inclusive, any change to the Aeroplan program that materially worsens conditions for members — specifically: (a) an increase to published award pricing bands, (b) a reduction in any published partner transfer ratio (both into and out of Aeroplan), (c) a reduction in earning rates on Aeroplan-issued or partner-issued flights, or (d) an increase to Aeroplan Elite qualification thresholds. GRADE MISS if any such change is publicly announced in that window, evidenced by Aeroplan's own page or an Air Canada media release plus a Tier 1 or Tier 2 confirmation.

calls.call: Marriott Bonvoy will publicly launch a Q4 2026 global earning promotion — with registration open to members on or before 2026-09-22 — that materially matches the LoyaltyLobby leak: a base offer of at least 1,000 bonus points for paid stays of two or more nights, plus an additional resort-property bonus component, with a stay window falling within Sept 22 – Nov 30, 2026.
calls.basis: LoyaltyLobby leaked the Q4 2026 Marriott promotion in early August: registration ~Sept 9, stay window Sept 22 – Nov 22, 1,500 base bonus points for 2+ night paid stays, extra 3,000 points at resorts. Marriott has publicly launched a Q4 global earning promotion in every year since 2019, and leaked-terms-then-official-launch is the normal Marriott pattern — the leak's structural shape (base + resort component + ~9-week stay window opening late September) has been consistent across five straight Q4 promos. A missed launch, or terms materially weaker than the leak, would signal Marriott is holding back Q4 generosity in a year that has already seen a 5–10% award-chart devaluation and a persistent flash devaluation trickle. The test resolves cleanly by Sept 22, the leaked stay-window start.
calls.test: GRADE HIT if Marriott Bonvoy publicly launches a Q4 2026 global earning promotion with registration open to members on or before 2026-09-22, offering a base of at least 1,000 bonus points for paid stays of two or more nights, plus an additional resort-property bonus component of any size, with a stay window that falls within 2026-09-22 through 2026-11-30 inclusive, evidenced by marriott.com/loyalty (Tier 1) or a Tier 1/Tier 2 confirmation. GRADE MISS if no such promo is publicly launched by 2026-09-22, OR if the promo launched by that date has a base of less than 1,000 bonus points for a 2+ night paid stay, OR lacks any resort-property bonus component.
calls.evidence: Marriott officially launched its Q4 2026 global promotion on 2026-09-09 with registration open through 2026-11-13 and a stay window of 2026-09-22 to 2026-11-22. Terms: 1,500 base bonus points for paid stays of 2+ nights plus an additional 3,000 bonus points at resort properties (4,500 max). All three test conditions met and confirmed by multiple Tier 2 sources; primary registration page: https://www.marriott.com/loyalty/promotion.mi?promotion=WL26

calls.call: The Amex Membership Rewards → Hilton Honors 30% bonus that launched today (Sept 1 – Oct 14, 2026) will be the ONLY Amex→Hilton transfer bonus publicly offered before 2027-01-31 — no additional Amex→Hilton bonus of any percentage will run between 2026-10-15 and 2027-01-31 inclusive.
calls.basis: Amex→Hilton bonuses have run roughly 1–2 times per calendar year, not consecutively. Recent cadence shows Amex clearing the Hilton box for the fall/holiday season with a single Q3–Q4 promo, then leaving the route quiet for 5–8 months. A repeat within 3.5 months of today's launch would break a multi-year pattern. Additionally, Hilton points are Amex's least valuable per-point hotel transfer destination (0.5–0.6 cents vs Marriott ~0.7 and Choice / partner airline transfers well above); Amex has less commercial incentive to promote heavily on this route once the seasonal box is checked.
calls.test: GRADE HIT if no Amex Membership Rewards → Hilton Honors transfer bonus of any percentage is publicly offered at any point between 2026-10-15 and 2027-01-31 inclusive. GRADE MISS if any such bonus is offered in that window, evidenced by Amex's own transfer page and confirmed by at least one Tier 1 or Tier 2 source.

calls.call: Flying Blue will NOT publicly announce any member-negative change to its partner-airline award pricing (SkyTeam partners plus Etihad, GOL, Kenya Airways, and other non-AF/KLM partners) between 2026-09-02 and 2027-01-31 inclusive.
calls.basis: The September 8, 2026 direct-airline tiered fares rollout (Light/Standard/Flex on AF and KLM direct awards) is publicly framed as changes that 'apply exclusively to travel on Air France and KLM, and not to travel on partner airlines, where pricing remains unchanged.' Programs that publicly split direct vs partner pricing at rollout typically preserve partner protection for 6–12 months; reversing that language inside 5 months would validate the 'bait-and-switch' critique during exactly the tiered-fare adoption phase when Flying Blue most needs member trust. Historical Flying Blue partner-chart changes have arrived on 12–24 month cycles, not clustered with direct-airline changes. Contrarian call — the loud fear on trade sites is that partner pricing is next; this bets it isn't, inside five months.
calls.test: GRADE HIT if no Flying Blue announcement, effective between 2026-09-02 and 2027-01-31 inclusive, materially worsens partner-airline award pricing (higher mile requirements on any published partner route, removed sweet spots such as intra-Europe short-haul, or a partner removed from the transfer roster). GRADE MISS if any such change is publicly announced in that window, evidenced by Flying Blue's own award page or an AF/KLM press release plus a Tier 1 or Tier 2 confirmation.

calls.call: Bilt Rewards will publicly launch at least one Bilt Rewards → Alaska/Hawaiian Atmos Rewards transfer bonus of 20% or greater between 2026-09-03 and 2027-01-31 inclusive.
calls.basis: Alaska Air Group completed the operational consolidation of HawaiianMiles and Mileage Plan into a single Atmos Rewards balance on 2026-08-14, and Bilt remains the only major flexible-points program with a direct transfer route in — with Amex closed since June 2025 and no Chase/Citi/Capital One partnership in flight (see call 2026-08-29-1). Bilt's monthly Rent Day cadence gives it four dedicated promo slots between now and end of January, and Atmos is the single highest-value differentiator Bilt can lean on against Chase or Amex. Alaska loyalty leadership has publicly framed banks as 'ultimately competitors', which reinforces Bilt's exclusivity moat and gives Alaska commercial incentive to reward Bilt with elevated promo terms. A five-month silence on Bilt's most distinctive transfer partner immediately after Atmos launched would waste the marketing moment; a bonus in the Sep-Jan window is the base case.
calls.test: GRADE HIT if any Bilt Rewards → Alaska/Hawaiian Atmos Rewards transfer bonus of 20% or greater is publicly offered at any point between 2026-09-03 and 2027-01-31 inclusive, evidenced by Bilt's own transfer page, an Alaska/Atmos promo page, or a Tier 1/Tier 2 confirmation. GRADE MISS if no such bonus is offered from Bilt to Atmos in that window.

calls.call: Amex Membership Rewards will run at least one transfer bonus of 25% or greater to Air France/KLM Flying Blue between 2026-09-04 and 2027-01-31 inclusive.
calls.basis: Flying Blue's September 8, 2026 tiered-fare rollout raises the effective mile cost of a Standard AF/KLM direct award to roughly 75,000 miles one-way in business (up from ~60,000 at the old entry level) — a de-facto 25% Standard-fare devaluation on the routes Amex members transfer most heavily to. Amex has run Membership Rewards → Flying Blue bonuses roughly twice a year on a steady cadence (most recently a 30% bonus in March 2026 and a 25% in June 2025), and post-devaluation windows are historically prime bonus periods as the source program smooths the effective cut for its members. Amex has commercial incentive to keep its most-transferred European partner attractive relative to Citi, which has already re-established quarterly Flying Blue cadence. A five-month silence spanning the exact post-devaluation adoption window would break both Amex's own cadence and the historical pattern of partner-devaluation → bank bonus response.
calls.test: GRADE HIT if any Amex Membership Rewards → Air France/KLM Flying Blue transfer bonus of 25% or greater is publicly offered at any point between 2026-09-04 and 2027-01-31 inclusive, evidenced by Amex's own transfer page, Flying Blue's promo page, or a Tier 1/Tier 2 confirmation. GRADE MISS if no such bonus is offered in that window.

calls.call: Amex Membership Rewards will publicly offer a transfer bonus of 20% or greater to Marriott Bonvoy between 2026-09-05 and 2026-11-15 inclusive.
calls.basis: Marriott's leaked Q4 2026 global earning promotion (LoyaltyLobby, registration Sept 9, stay window Sept 22 – Nov 22) creates aligned commercial incentive on the earn side for Amex to run a smoothing points-refill bonus in the same window — the classic handshake between hotel earn-promo and bank transfer-promo has repeated in Q4 2023, Q4 2024 (Amex→Marriott 20% Oct 22 – Nov 20), and Q4 2025. Amex's last MR→Marriott bonus was a 20% offer in April 2026 (Apr 8 – May 5); a six-month gap through October fits Amex's typical semi-annual Marriott cadence. Amex has commercial pressure to compete with Chase's fall hotel promos and needs a Q4 hotel bonus once its Hilton box is checked. The horizon lands on Nov 15 to catch either an October launch (matching 2024) or a November launch (matching 2025), while giving a clean 10-week resolution window.
calls.test: GRADE HIT if any Amex Membership Rewards → Marriott Bonvoy transfer bonus of 20% or greater is publicly offered at any point between 2026-09-05 and 2026-11-15 inclusive, evidenced by Amex's own transfer page, Marriott's promo page, or a Tier 1/Tier 2 confirmation. GRADE MISS if no such bonus is offered in that window.

calls.call: Rove Miles will either extend its current 40% Rove → Copa Airlines ConnectMiles transfer bonus past 2026-09-30, OR publicly launch a follow-up Rove → Copa transfer bonus of 20% or greater between 2026-10-01 and 2026-12-31 inclusive.
calls.basis: Copa Airlines ConnectMiles went live as a Rove transfer partner on September 1, 2026, with a launch 40% bonus at 1:1.4 running through September 30 at 11:59pm EST. New-partner launch promos of this size are marketing investments, not one-shot experiments — Rove needs to seed transfer volume through Q4 to prove the partnership is working and to convert new sign-ups it acquired during the Copa announcement cycle. A hard cutover from 40% to 0% at 30 days would signal Rove either overestimated launch demand or is in cost-control mode, both of which contradict its 2026 aggressive-partner-addition posture. Q4 is Latin America holiday-booking season, which is exactly when Copa ConnectMiles inbound transfer value peaks. A four-month silence on a marquee new partner during its natural high-demand window would waste the launch narrative.
calls.test: GRADE HIT if Rove either (a) extends the current 40% Rove → Copa ConnectMiles transfer bonus past 2026-09-30 in any form (same 40% extended, or any Rove → Copa bonus continuing into October), OR (b) publicly offers a follow-up Rove → Copa transfer bonus of 20% or greater at any point between 2026-10-01 and 2026-12-31 inclusive, evidenced by Rove's own blog, transfer page, or a Tier 1/Tier 2 confirmation. GRADE MISS if the current 40% bonus expires as scheduled on 2026-09-30 AND no follow-up Rove → Copa bonus of 20% or greater is offered between 2026-10-01 and 2026-12-31.

calls.call: No PUBLIC Amex Membership Rewards → Delta SkyMiles transfer bonus of any percentage will be broadly (non-targeted) offered between 2026-09-07 and 2027-01-31 inclusive.
calls.basis: Public Amex→Delta transfer bonuses are vanishingly rare. Delta is Amex's largest single co-brand relationship by revenue, and the two firms deliberately keep the flexible-transfer route quiet because promoting it would cannibalise Delta SkyMiles card acquisition (which pays Amex per-account and per-swipe economics that dwarf transfer margins). Occasional targeted transfer bonuses have appeared in individual Amex accounts historically, but a broadly announced public bonus has not run in years. The loud consensus after Delta's 2024–2025 SkyMiles devaluations is that Amex should sweeten the transfer route to keep members holding SkyMiles balances; this call bets that the co-brand economics prevail and Amex stays quiet through the winter transfer window. A first public Amex→Delta bonus in five months would signal a genuine strategy shift, not just a promo cycle.
calls.test: GRADE HIT if no PUBLIC (broadly announced, non-targeted) Amex Membership Rewards → Delta SkyMiles transfer bonus of any percentage is publicly offered at any point between 2026-09-07 and 2027-01-31 inclusive. GRADE MISS if any such publicly announced Amex→Delta bonus (>0%) runs during that window, evidenced by Amex's own transfer page and confirmed by at least one Tier 1 or Tier 2 source (targeted mailings or account-only offers do not count).

calls.call: Within 30 days of Flying Blue's September 8, 2026 tiered-fare rollout, at least one of Amex Membership Rewards, Chase Ultimate Rewards, Citi ThankYou, Capital One Miles, or Bilt Rewards will publicly launch a transfer bonus of 20% or greater to Air France/KLM Flying Blue — a smoothing response to the direct-award devaluation.
calls.basis: Historically, bank programs respond to partner-airline devaluations with smoothing bonuses during the adoption window, because member trust in the source program erodes when a headline destination cuts value while transfer economics stay flat. Amex has the strongest cadence to Flying Blue (30% in March 2026, 25% in June 2025) and its Membership Rewards-to-Flying Blue route has now gone six months quiet — the exact silence a Q4 push would break. Citi's own Flying Blue quarterly cadence next opens roughly early-to-mid November, outside this 30-day window, which effectively makes this call a bet on Amex specifically stepping into the vacuum inside a month. Bilt has run Flying Blue Rent Day bonuses at 100% historically and has a September 30 Rent Day slot open. This is a short-horizon, high-topicality call: if the historical pattern holds, at least one of the five will move fast; if none does, the 'bank smooths partner devaluations' rule is weaker than the industry assumes.
calls.test: GRADE HIT if any of Amex Membership Rewards, Chase Ultimate Rewards, Citi ThankYou, Capital One Miles, or Bilt Rewards publicly offers a transfer bonus of 20% or greater to Air France/KLM Flying Blue at any point between 2026-09-08 and 2026-10-08 inclusive, evidenced by that program's own transfer page, Flying Blue's promo page, or a Tier 1/Tier 2 confirmation. GRADE MISS if no such bonus is offered from any of those five programs in that window.

calls.call: Chase Ultimate Rewards will NOT run another UR → Marriott Bonvoy transfer bonus of 50% or greater between 2026-10-16 and 2027-04-15 inclusive — the current 70% bonus (Sep 15 – Oct 15, 2026) is a one-off headline event, not the start of a new elevated cadence.
calls.basis: Multiple Tier 2 sources (The Points Guy, One Mile at a Time, LoyaltyLobby, Frequent Miler, Upgraded Points) explicitly describe the current 70% offer as the highest-ever Chase→Marriott bonus. Historical Chase→Marriott bonuses have topped out around 25–50%, most recently in Q4 2024. Chase's Q4 2026 hotel push appears to be split between IHG (70%, July–August) and Marriott (70%, Sep–Oct) — both concentrated in the second half of the year rather than repeated. Marriott's May 2026 award-chart devaluation and persistent flash devaluation trickle already make the transfer route economically weaker than headline percentages suggest, and repeating a record-high bonus inside six months would either compound Marriott's revenue leak or signal deeper commercial pressure than currently visible. A repeat at 50%+ inside six months would break the observed once-per-year cadence of elevated Chase→Marriott bonuses.
calls.test: GRADE HIT if no Chase Ultimate Rewards → Marriott Bonvoy transfer bonus of 50% or greater is publicly offered at any point between 2026-10-16 and 2027-04-15 inclusive. GRADE MISS if any such bonus (≥50%) is announced or live during that window, evidenced by Chase's own transfer page and confirmed by at least one Tier 1 or Tier 2 source. GRADE UNSETTLED if Chase runs a Chase→Marriott bonus of 40–49% in that window (the record bar remains intact even if activity is elevated).

calls.call: Neither Amex Membership Rewards nor Citi ThankYou will publicly launch a transfer bonus of 25% or greater to Marriott Bonvoy between 2026-09-17 and 2026-10-15 inclusive — Chase's record 70% Chase→Marriott bonus (Sep 15 – Oct 15, 2026) will not trigger an in-window competitive response from other transferable-points programs.
calls.basis: Amex and Citi run hotel bonuses on their own cadences, not reactively. Amex's last MR→Marriott bonus was a 20% offer in April 2026 (Apr 8–May 5), and its typical semi-annual Marriott rhythm points to an October or November launch — landing outside or right at the edge of Chase's window. Citi ThankYou→Marriott bonuses are historically infrequent (last meaningful public offer: 25% in 2023) and Citi's Q4 promo focus has consistently been airlines (Turkish, Flying Blue) rather than hotels. On the sell side, Marriott and Chase co-invested in the record 70% promo; Marriott would not simultaneously undercut it with an equal-or-better Amex or Citi bonus during the same 30-day window. A rival 25%+ MR→Marriott or TY→Marriott bonus inside Chase's window would be a genuine strategic response — the historical base rate says it does not happen.
calls.test: GRADE HIT if no Amex Membership Rewards → Marriott Bonvoy transfer bonus of 25% or greater AND no Citi ThankYou → Marriott Bonvoy transfer bonus of 25% or greater is publicly offered at any point between 2026-09-17 and 2026-10-15 inclusive. GRADE MISS if either program publicly offers a 25%+ transfer bonus to Marriott in that window, evidenced by that program's own transfer page and confirmed by at least one Tier 1 or Tier 2 source.

calls.call: Chase will NOT publicly walk back, extend, or grace-period the World of Hyatt 4:3 transfer devaluation for Chase Sapphire Preferred or Ink Business Preferred existing cardholders past its announced October 1, 2026 cutover date — the devaluation lands as scheduled and stays landed through 2026-10-31.
calls.basis: Since the June 15, 2026 Chase Sapphire Preferred refresh announcement, Frequent Miler, One Mile at a Time and The Points Guy have all run 'last chance' pieces pressuring Chase to reconsider — pressure that has been amplified over the last two weeks as the deadline nears. Chase has never once, in a documented product-refresh cycle, rolled back a scheduled negative change on a hitherto sacrosanct route once it publicly announced both a date and a segmentation carve-out (Sapphire Reserve and Sapphire Reserve for Business retain 1:1). That carve-out is itself Chase's answer to the 'you're devaluing your best customers' complaint; extending 1:1 to Sapphire Preferred would collapse the segmentation Chase just paid to introduce. Existing Sapphire Preferred cardholders got ~110 days of advance notice — longer than the industry's typical 30–60 day negative-change window — which further reduces Chase's legal or reputational exposure to a rollback. Contrarian angle: the loud consensus on trade sites is 'transfer now while you can'; this call bets the deadline holds.
calls.test: GRADE HIT if, at any point between 2026-10-01 and 2026-10-31 inclusive, the effective Chase Ultimate Rewards → World of Hyatt transfer ratio for Chase Sapphire Preferred and Ink Business Preferred existing cardholders is 4:3 (i.e., 1,000 UR → 750 Hyatt points) as originally announced, evidenced by Chase's own Ultimate Rewards transfer page or a Tier 1/Tier 2 confirmation. GRADE MISS if Chase publicly announces or implements any extension, grace period, rollback, or continued 1:1 rate for Chase Sapphire Preferred or Ink Business Preferred existing cardholders past 2026-10-01, evidenced by Chase's own communication and confirmed by at least one Tier 1 or Tier 2 source.

calls.call: Chase will NOT change the base Ultimate Rewards → Marriott Bonvoy transfer ratio OR the base Ultimate Rewards → IHG One Rewards transfer ratio from 1:1 for any consumer or business Chase Ultimate Rewards-earning credit card at any point between 2026-09-19 and 2026-12-31 inclusive.
calls.basis: The October 1 Chase→Hyatt 4:3 cut is a targeted segmentation move — Sapphire Reserve and Sapphire Reserve for Business keep 1:1, meaning Chase is deliberately carving Hyatt transfer value as a premium-tier benefit rather than repricing hotels wholesale. Marriott Bonvoy and IHG One Rewards are much less valuable per-point transfer partners than Hyatt (Hyatt ~2c/pt vs Marriott ~0.7c/pt and IHG ~0.5c/pt), so the economic case for a further consumer-tier haircut is far weaker. Running a record-high 70% UR→Marriott bonus RIGHT NOW alongside a base ratio cut on the same partner would be commercially incoherent, and Chase gave 110 days of advance notice on the Hyatt change — that runway is uncharacteristic of a program planning back-to-back ratio cuts. A second consumer-tier hotel ratio cut inside a single quarter would provoke a much louder backlash than the Hyatt move already has.
calls.test: GRADE HIT if the base Chase Ultimate Rewards → Marriott Bonvoy transfer ratio remains 1:1 AND the base Chase Ultimate Rewards → IHG One Rewards transfer ratio remains 1:1 for all consumer and business Chase Ultimate Rewards-earning credit cards at every point between 2026-09-19 and 2026-12-31 inclusive, evidenced by Chase's own Ultimate Rewards transfer page. GRADE MISS if either base ratio is publicly changed to anything other than 1:1 (for any Chase UR-earning card, whether or not premium tiers are carved out) at any point in that window, evidenced by Chase's own transfer page and confirmed by at least one Tier 1 or Tier 2 source.

calls.call: Bilt Rewards will publicly launch a Bilt Rewards to World of Hyatt transfer bonus of 25% or greater between 2026-10-01 and 2026-11-30 inclusive - a Rent Day competitive response to Chase's Sapphire Preferred / Ink Business Preferred 4:3 Hyatt devaluation that lands on October 1, 2026.
calls.basis: Bilt is one of only two major flexible-points programs with an active World of Hyatt transfer route (the other being Chase); Amex, Citi, and Capital One do not transfer to Hyatt at all. October 1 is the exact day Chase's Sapphire Preferred and Ink Preferred cardholders lose their 1:1 rate to Hyatt while Bilt keeps 1:1 on every card. That is a fully-primed competitive asymmetry, and Bilt's monthly Rent Day cadence gives it two dedicated promo slots inside the 60-day window. Bilt has an established pattern of running Rent Day bonuses to differentiated aspirational partners immediately after competitor moves (the September 2026 Virgin Atlantic Rent Day at up to 100% is the current template). A 60-day silence on Bilt's most valuable exclusive-vs-Chase lever during the exact 60 days when Chase is publicly penalising Preferred cardholders on the same partner would waste the marketing moment.
calls.test: GRADE HIT if any Bilt Rewards to World of Hyatt transfer bonus of 25% or greater is publicly offered at any point between 2026-10-01 and 2026-11-30 inclusive, evidenced by Bilt's own transfer page, a Hyatt promo page, or a Tier 1/Tier 2 confirmation. GRADE MISS if no such bonus is offered from Bilt to World of Hyatt in that window.

calls.call: The Citi ThankYou to Japan Airlines Mileage Bank launch bonus (30% through 2026-10-24) will NOT be extended past its stated end date, AND no follow-up Citi ThankYou to JAL Mileage Bank transfer bonus of any percentage will be publicly offered between 2026-10-25 and 2027-01-24 inclusive.
calls.basis: Citi added JAL as a 1:1 transfer partner on 2026-09-20 with a 30% launch promo running through Oct 24. New-partner launch bonuses at flexible-points programs are marketing spikes, not the start of a cadence: Chase's Emirates launch (2023), Amex's Aeroplan launch (2020), and Bilt's various new-partner launches all ran once at elevated terms and then went quiet for six-plus months while transfer-volume economics stabilised. Citi's own cadence to established 1:1 partners (Flying Blue, LifeMiles, Turkish) sits at 3-4 months from bonus-end to next-bonus; on a brand-new partner where unit economics are still being measured, that gap is expected to be longer, not shorter. A repeat inside 90 days would signal Citi is aggressively fighting for JAL transfer share against Capital One (which has a competing JAL 30% ending Sept 30) rather than establishing rhythm - a strategic move, not a cadence signal.
calls.test: GRADE HIT if the current 30% Citi ThankYou to JAL Mileage Bank transfer bonus expires as scheduled on 2026-10-24 without extension, AND no follow-up Citi ThankYou to JAL Mileage Bank transfer bonus of any percentage greater than zero is publicly offered at any point between 2026-10-25 and 2027-01-24 inclusive. GRADE MISS if the current 30% is extended past 2026-10-24, OR if any follow-up Citi to JAL bonus greater than zero is publicly offered in that window, evidenced by Citi's own transfer page and confirmed by at least one Tier 1 or Tier 2 source.

calls.call: Amex Membership Rewards will NOT add Japan Airlines Mileage Bank as a publicly listed transfer partner at any point between 2026-09-22 and 2027-03-22 inclusive.
calls.basis: Citi added JAL as its 24th airline partner on 2026-09-20, joining Capital One (which added JAL in 2022) and the indirect Marriott→JAL route as the flexible-points paths in. Amex's transfer stack has been notably stable for years — the most recent airline partner change was subtractive (Amex closed the Hawaiian route on 2025-06-30). More structurally, Amex's largest US airline co-brand relationship by revenue is Delta, and Delta and JAL are SkyTeam-adjacent rivals in the trans-Pacific premium market: adding JAL as an Amex transfer partner would either cannibalise Delta SkyMiles card acquisition or require SkyMiles-side concessions from Delta that Amex has no historical pattern of extracting. JAL's own US bank-partnership expansion has been deliberately paced (Marriott 2015, Capital One 2022, Citi 2026-09-20); a 4th major-bank addition within 6 months would break JAL's observed cadence. A six-month horizon covers any post-Citi-launch experimentation window.
calls.test: GRADE HIT if Amex Membership Rewards does not publicly list Japan Airlines Mileage Bank as an active transfer partner at any point between 2026-09-22 and 2027-03-22 inclusive. GRADE MISS if Amex publicly lists JAL Mileage Bank as a transfer partner (at any transfer ratio) at any point in that window, evidenced by Amex's own transfer page and confirmed by at least one Tier 1 or Tier 2 source.

calls.call: Capital One will publicly launch another Capital One miles → JAL Mileage Bank transfer bonus of 20% or greater between 2026-10-01 and 2027-02-28 inclusive — a defensive response to Citi's September 20, 2026 launch of JAL as a 1:1 transfer partner.
calls.basis: Capital One added JAL as a transfer partner in 2022 and has run periodic JAL bonuses since then; the current 30% bonus (Sept 1 – Sept 30, 2026, ending in seven days) is the third Cap One → JAL promo in the last 18 months. On September 20, 2026 Citi ThankYou went live with JAL as a brand-new 1:1 partner alongside a 30% launch bonus running through October 24 — direct competitive pressure on the exact route Cap One has spent three years cultivating. A five-month silence immediately after a rival's launch bonus would cede JAL transfer share Cap One has structurally invested in, and Q4 through Q1 is historically Cap One's most active bonus window as it competes with Amex and Citi for year-end transfer volume. Cap One's own JAL cadence has averaged roughly one promo per quarter through 2025-2026. The horizon lands at Feb 28 to catch either a Q4 defensive push against Citi's Oct 24 bonus expiry OR a Q1 cadence bonus, while giving a clean five-month resolution window.
calls.test: GRADE HIT if any Capital One miles → JAL Mileage Bank transfer bonus of 20% or greater is publicly offered at any point between 2026-10-01 and 2027-02-28 inclusive, evidenced by Capital One's own transfer page, a JAL promo page, or a Tier 1/Tier 2 confirmation. GRADE MISS if no such bonus is offered in that window.
